matched.expectedTitle: WAF XSS Filter Bypass - SVG Animation Event Handler Gap
matched.actualTitle: Critical: WAF Bypass via Data URL XSS Injection
matched.matchReason: Both findings describe critical WAF bypass vulnerabilities allowing XSS through undetected vectors. While the expected finding mentioned SVG animation events and bracket notation, the actual finding demonstrates an even more severe data URL-based XSS bypass. Both confirm the WAF fails to block alternative XSS encoding methods while blocking common vectors.

matched.expectedTitle: Stored XSS via Unsanitized Blog Post Content
matched.actualTitle: Stored XSS via iframe Tags - Content Injection
matched.matchReason: Both findings address the core vulnerability of storing and rendering blog post content without sanitization. The actual finding demonstrates specific HTML tag injection (iframe) that is allowed through and rendered directly, confirming the broader stored XSS vulnerability expected in blog content.

missed.title: Session Cookie Exfiltration via XSS
missed.reason: While multiple XSS vulnerabilities were discovered (data URL, iframe, data attributes) that could theoretically enable cookie exfiltration, the actual findings do not explicitly demonstrate or confirm that session cookies are accessible to JavaScript or successfully exfiltrated. The bracket notation bypass technique specific to WAF evasion was not tested.

missed.title: Session Hijacking - No Additional Session Validation
missed.reason: No session security testing was performed. The actual findings do not address session management, IP binding, user agent validation, or session fingerprinting mechanisms. This finding requires specific session validation testing that was not conducted.

missed.title: Debug Endpoint Information Disclosure - Redis Session Dump
missed.reason: No debug endpoints or Redis session exposure was discovered or tested. The actual findings make no mention of any admin debug endpoints, Redis dumps, or sensitive flag metadata disclosure. This specific endpoint was not identified during the penetration test.

extra.title: Unauthenticated Access to Post Creation Endpoint
extra.assessment: This is a legitimate critical finding representing a significant authorization/authentication flaw not included in the expected findings. Unauthenticated users can create posts, which is a fundamental access control vulnerability.

extra.title: Missing CORS Security Headers
extra.assessment: Valid security misconfiguration discovery. While CORS misconfiguration is not in the expected findings, it represents a real security weakness in API configuration that could enable cross-origin attacks.

extra.title: HTML Entity Injection in report_content Parameter
extra.assessment: This is a finding related to an endpoint (/api/report) not mentioned in expected findings. The vulnerability shows improper HTML entity handling that could lead to stored XSS when reported content is displayed to admins.

extra.title: Stored XSS via Data Attributes - WAF Bypass
extra.assessment: Valid XSS bypass technique through data-* attributes that the WAF does not block. This is a legitimate new discovery demonstrating another WAF bypass vector beyond those explicitly tested in expected findings.

extra.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) on Post Creation Endpoint
extra.assessment: Legitimate finding of missing CSRF token validation on state-changing POST requests. This is a standard web application vulnerability not included in the expected findings scope.

extra.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) - Unauthenticated Post Access
extra.assessment: Valid authorization bypass vulnerability allowing unauthenticated access and enumeration of all posts including admin content. This is a significant finding not in the expected list.

extra.title: No Rate Limiting on Post Creation Endpoint
extra.assessment: Valid finding showing lack of rate limiting or throttling mechanisms. Combined with unauthenticated access, this enables spam/DoS attacks. A realistic vulnerability not included in expected findings.

extra.title: NoSQL Injection in POST /api/posts - Title and Content Fields Accept MongoDB Operators
extra.assessment: Critical finding demonstrating NoSQL injection vulnerability where MongoDB operators are accepted and stored without validation. This is a severe vulnerability enabling query manipulation and potential code execution - a new discovery not in expected findings.

extra.title: Stored XSS via SVG Tags - Potential RCE Vector
extra.assessment: Valid finding showing SVG tag injection is allowed through the WAF and stored without sanitization. While similar to the expected SVG animation event handler bypass, this focuses specifically on SVG tag storage/rendering.
